question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q5b — Induced Current: Direction and Magnitude Table
question.text:
Three figures (Figures 7, 8, and 9) show a bar magnet and a coil connected to an ammeter with terminals A and B.

  • Figure 7: The magnet is moved towards the coil at TWICE the original speed.
  • Figure 8: The magnet is moved away from the coil at TWICE the original speed.
  • Figure 9: The magnet is held stationary inside the coil.

Complete Table 2 to show the direction of the induced current through the ammeter and the change in the magnitude of the current compared with the original.

FigureDirection of induced currentChange in magnitude

question.general_feedback:
Electromagnetic induction — key principles:

Faraday's Law: The magnitude of the induced EMF is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux. Faster movement or a stronger field → greater induced EMF and current.

Lenz's Law: The direction of the induced current opposes the change causing it (like a braking force).

FigureScenarioDirectionMagnitude change
Fig 7N-pole moved TOWARD coil at 2× speedA→BDoubles (2× original speed → 2× rate of flux change)
Fig 8N-pole moved AWAY from coil at 2× speedB→ADoubles (moving away reverses direction; same speed as Fig 7)
Fig 9Magnet STATIONARY inside coilNone (no current)Unchanged — remains zero (no flux change → no induced EMF)

Why direction reverses in Fig 8: Moving the magnet away reduces the flux through the coil — the induced current flows in the opposite direction to oppose this decrease (Lenz's Law).

steps.label:
Faraday's Law: EMF ∝ rate of change of flux  |  Faster speed → greater EMF/current
Lenz's Law: Induced current opposes the change causing it → direction reverses when magnet moves away
Complete Fig 7 row: magnet moved toward coil at 2× speed. (2 marks)
Complete Fig 8 row: magnet moved away from coil at 2× speed. (2 marks)
Complete Fig 9 row: magnet stationary inside coil. (2 marks)

fields.label: Fig 7 — direction of induced current
fields.diagnostic_hint: When the N-pole moves toward the coil, the induced current flows A→B (by Lenz's Law, opposing the increasing flux).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Fig 7: N-pole moves TOWARD coil → flux through coil increases → induced current flows in the direction that opposes the increase → current direction is A→B through the external ammeter.

fields.label: Fig 7 — change in magnitude compared with original
fields.diagnostic_hint: Moving at twice the speed doubles the rate of flux change, so by Faraday's Law the induced EMF and current double.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Faraday's Law: induced EMF ∝ rate of change of magnetic flux. Moving at 2× the original speed doubles the rate of flux change → the induced current doubles.

fields.label: Fig 8 — direction of induced current
fields.diagnostic_hint: When the N-pole moves away from the coil, the flux is decreasing, so the induced current reverses direction: B→A.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Fig 8: N-pole moves AWAY from coil → flux decreases → Lenz's Law says induced current opposes the decrease → current reverses direction compared to Fig 7 → current is B→A.

fields.label: Fig 8 — change in magnitude compared with original
fields.diagnostic_hint: Moving away at 2× speed also doubles the rate of flux change — same magnitude increase as Fig 7, just reversed direction.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Fig 8: same speed (2× original) as Fig 7, so the magnitude of the induced current is also doubled. Only the direction differs.

fields.label: Fig 9 — direction of induced current
fields.diagnostic_hint: A stationary magnet produces no change in flux → no induced EMF → no current flows.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Fig 9: magnet is stationary → no change in magnetic flux through the coil → no induced EMF (Faraday's Law: EMF = 0 when rate of flux change = 0) → no current flows.

fields.label: Fig 9 — change in magnitude compared with original
fields.diagnostic_hint: No current flows in Fig 9 — the magnitude is zero/unchanged from the stationary baseline.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Fig 9: stationary magnet → no induced current → the magnitude is unchanged at zero. There is no current to have a magnitude.
